# got-a.page

> Free community subdomains for profiles, products, projects and communities. Claim a name.got-a.page address with a pull request.

got-a.page offers two ways to publish a page:
- **Instant mode:** got-a.page hosts a simple profile or product page. No separate hosting setup is required.
- **Point mode:** use a got-a.page subdomain with a site hosted elsewhere by configuring supported DNS records.

## Getting started

- Choose a name with the guided claim form, which creates the page JSON and opens the claim repository on GitHub.
- Claims are proposed as pull requests in the claim repository and are checked before merge.
- Each GitHub account can currently claim up to two pages. Names are 2–40 characters using lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, without hyphens at either edge.
- Instant-mode pages generally publish within a few minutes after the claim pull request is merged.
- For point mode, add the subdomain to your hosting provider before the claim is merged. DNS propagation and HTTPS certificate issuance can take additional time after merge.
- The service is free. Page configuration is public in the community repository; do not include private information.

## Canonical pages

- [Homepage](https://got-a.page/): overview and name availability checker.
- [Documentation and FAQ](https://got-a.page/docs): claiming, instant mode, point mode, host setup, post-merge timing and troubleshooting.
- [Claim form](https://got-a.page/claim): guided form for creating a page claim.
- [Badges](https://got-a.page/badges/): project badges.

## Source repositories

- [Website source](https://github.com/got-a-page/website): static website, documentation and claim form.
- [Claim repository](https://github.com/got-a-page/claim): page definitions and claim pull requests.
- [got-a.page organization](https://github.com/got-a-page): project repositories and community activity.

## Further guidance

Use the documentation as the canonical source for setup steps, supported DNS records, rules and troubleshooting. Do not infer that a point-mode domain is ready immediately after merge; confirm DNS and HTTPS at the hosting provider.
